transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-02 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Luca Romano, Priya Desai (Redwood); Daniel Kim, Sofia Alvarez, Marcus Lee, Priya Patel (Vertex)
Links shared: telemetry dashboard (https://redwood.app/telemetry/vertex-csv), pilot plan doc (internal link), packet capture dropbox note

Summary (auto): Weekly POC check-in. Main discussion centered on last night's kernel/quant upgrade and its effect on p95 tail latency. Action items assigned for telemetry enrichment, targeted p95 test, and security artefact review.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining — we'll go about 45 minutes. Quick roll call?
[00:07] Daniel Kim: hi, daniel here, head of ML at Vertex.
[00:10] Sofia Alvarez: sophia, infra.
[00:12] Marcus Lee: marcus from security.
[00:14] Priya Patel: priya, SRE.
[00:16] Maya Chen: great. from redwood we have luca and priya desai. luca, quick status on the kernel upgrade?
[00:23] Luca Romano: yeah so we rolled the quantized kernel at 02:00 UTC last night across the private nodes in us-east-1a and 1b, it was staged canary then full. avg token latency dropped about 12% overall which is good, cost per token improved, but p95 spiked in three 5-to-8 minute windows — looks correlated with KV cache misses and cross-AZ fallback routing.
[00:42] Daniel Kim: correct, we saw the same. the average looks pretty, uh, improved, but those spikes are what worry product; they see timeouts on critical checkout flows.
[00:50] Sofia Alvarez: we noticed an increase in egress retries at the same timestamps. packet captures attached in the doc show reordering and some small bursts. could be our network shaping interacting with the new kernel's batching heuristics.
[01:10] Maya Chen: interesting, so two axes: the runtime change and the infra network shaping. Luca, do you have a hypothesis how the quantized path would increase cache misses?
[01:20] Luca Romano: yeah—so quantization changes memory layout for KV cache pages, on some models we saw slightly higher eviction rates because the framework proactively sizes the per-request KV allocation differently. usually caching behavior improves with quantization but edge cases where sequence lengths vary a lot can cause more cache churn.
[01:38] Daniel Kim: our workloads have a bimodal sequence length distribution — short queries for product search and long for personalized recommendations — maybe that's it.
[01:45] Priya Patel: we can simulate with our p95 synthetic workload but we need the exact cache sizing parameters you used.
[01:52] Luca Romano: noted — we'll share the kernel config and the cache tuning we shipped.
[01:56] Maya Chen: ok action: luca to share config.
[02:00] Marcus Lee: on security — any change in encryption or KMS usage with the quant kernel? we need to update our compliance tracker.
[02:08] Priya Desai: no change to key handling; KMS is untouched. the kernel change is purely execution/quantization. however, telemetry traces now include a slightly different trace id format in a couple fields — that might affect your log parsers.
[02:24] Marcus Lee: please put that in writing. we need to know if the trace IDs change schema.
[02:28] Priya Desai: will do.
[02:30] Maya Chen: Sofia, you mentioned egress shaping — can you explain current shaping policy?
[02:35] Sofia Alvarez: yes, we have a per-AZ egress limiter to keep costs bounded — it smooths bursts by queuing. during the spikes, the queueing delay + re-routing when a node fails over to another AZ looked to add around 80-120ms which pushed p95 over threshold.
[02:53] Daniel Kim: so basically combination of more cache misses, batching behavior that waits a few ms to fill, plus our egress queueing — triple whammy.
[03:02] Luca Romano: exactly; the runtime can be tuned to reduce batching latency for low-latency routes, and we can add a policy to prefer same-AZ routing for critical routes to avoid cross-AZ egress unless absolutely necessary.
[03:15] Priya Patel: if we prefer same-AZ, what happens during node drain or maintenance? do you have fallback quickly enough?
[03:21] Luca Romano: we do; fallback exists but is slower. we can reduce the fallback timeout to speed failover detection, but that increases risk of false positives and more frequent fallbacks. it's a tradeoff.
[03:33] Maya Chen: alright let's put a concrete experiment: reduce fallback timeout from 10s to 4s for the checkout route for a 2h window and measure p95 and error rate. agree?
[03:44] Daniel Kim: yes, we'll run it in the low-traffic slot Thursday 02:00-04:00 UTC.
[03:50] Sofia Alvarez: noted. we'll also capture packet traces and interface counters.
[03:54] Luca Romano: i'll add telemetry tags so we can filter the checkout route easily.
[03:58] Maya Chen: good. other telemetry gaps?
[04:01] Daniel Kim: we want per-route token breakdown by model version and the trace IDs that priya mentioned — currently the dashboard aggregates across routes so we can't see which model variant caused the spike.
[04:13] Priya Desai: understood — we can add per-route token counts and annotate model variant in the trace. luca to add per-route breakdown.
[04:20] Luca Romano: i'll do that and attach a CSV export link.
[04:24] Maya Chen: Marcus, security artefacts? what do you need to proceed with SOC2 scoping?
[04:29] Marcus Lee: three quick things: 1) KMS usage confirmation (you said unchanged) 2) audit log retention and access controls for private control plane 3) any third-party subprocesses that access token plaintext in logs.
[04:43] Priya Desai: private control plane has audit logs; retention can be configured. we do not persist token plaintext in logs; we emit token counts and hashed IDs.
[04:53] Marcus Lee: please send the specific retention windows and S3/RDS ACLs.
[04:58] Maya Chen: can you take that offline with Marcus, Priya?
[05:02] Priya Desai: yes, will do and share a short doc.
[05:06] Maya Chen: any regressions besides p95 spikes? errors, throughput?
[05:10] Daniel Kim: throughput steady, overall error rate slightly up during the three spike windows, but not sustained.
[05:16] Sofia Alvarez: also saw a small bump in CPU steal on the host during one incident; unclear if noisy neighbor or scheduling blip.
[05:24] Luca Romano: could be NPU driver interacting with quant kernel — on some hardware variants, quant ops offload to different kernels. we'll check telemetry for kernel scheduling events.
[05:34] Maya Chen: okay next we discussed a rollback plan if the targeted tests show regression. Luca?
[05:39] Luca Romano: we prepared a patch sequence: 1) revert quantized kernel on the affected node pool 2) if revert isn't sufficient, apply cache size bump 3) if persistent, pin model to full-precision variant for 24h. Rollback can be done within 20-30 minutes per pool.
[05:57] Daniel Kim: good to know. timeframe acceptable.
[06:00] Priya Patel: please flag us ahead of rollback so we can pause deployments.
[06:04] Maya Chen: will do.
[06:06] Marcus Lee: also propose we run a 2-hour controlled p95 test with synthetic load and realistic seq length mix so we can correlate traces with packet captures.
[06:16] Daniel Kim: already scheduled for Thu 02:00-04:00 UTC.
[06:20] Maya Chen: perfect. any blockers for SOC2 scoping?
[06:24] Marcus Lee: nothing blocking yet. just need the artefacts listed.
[06:28] Maya Chen: great. quick timings and owners recap.
[06:32] [10:30] -- natural pause while participants check doc links --
[06:40] Priya Desai: one more note — telemetry will now send a 'kernel_version' tag; older traces won't have it so when you look at historical compare, please be aware.
[06:53] Daniel Kim: noted — we'll adjust our parser.
[06:56] Maya Chen: ok let's close with concrete next steps and who does them.
[07:00] Luca Romano: luca will: share kernel config, add per-route token CSV, and tag checkout route for the Thu test (due 4/5).
[07:10] Sofia Alvarez: sophia will: run network egress shaping test and upload pcap (due 4/7).
[07:16] Marcus Lee: marcus will: send compliance Qs and schedule SOC2 scoping call (due 4/6).
[07:21] Maya Chen: maya will: send pricing appendix and pilot milestone contract (due 4/9).
[07:27] Daniel Kim: daniel — we'll run the Thu 02:00-04:00 UTC p95 run and share results.
[07:33] Priya Patel: priya will: watch for the rollback window and coordinate internal pauses.
[07:38] Maya Chen: awesome. any final Qs?
[07:41] Daniel Kim: no, thanks. appreciate the responsiveness.
[07:44] Maya Chen: thanks all — we'll follow up in the thread with links.
[07:48] -- meeting ends --
